links.outcome: Reading level (FRES) of publicly available ClinicalTrials.gov brief summaries for lay readers
links.effect: Original human-written summaries had mean FRES 17.0 ± 13.1, far below the recommended middle-school level, versus 73.3 ± 3.5 for GAI summaries (p < 0.0001).
links.quote: Brief summaries on ClinicalTrials.gov are indented for lay people, however are often written at a reading level that is too advanced for the public.

links.outcome: Readability and content completeness of GAI-generated layperson trial summaries
links.effect: GAI summaries had mean FRES 73.3 ± 3.5 (middle-school level), simpler syntax and reduced lexical complexity, and 100% inclusion of guideline-defined content elements.
links.quote: These findings suggest that GAI tools such as Pub2Post can generate patient-facing summaries that are both accessible and comprehensive.

unlisted_practices: Using generative AI to rewrite clinical trial registry summaries into plain language

screen.reason: Evaluates a generative AI tool (Pub2Post) for simplifying clinical trial summaries for patients, assessing readability and completeness offline against original summaries without testing a specific organizational deployment safeguard.
